answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 40% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the anchor calculation reruns each epoch, the nadir weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the pearl settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 45 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 22 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
